what_happened: sf1-engine's integration/project-link.md already names this task by slug in its own cross-repository register as an owed obligation, and its section 10 already states seven concrete rulings (Q39 origin/suggestion rule, gate M4 for a linked repo, per-session bound, attribution, 6-filter sharing policy, folder-move resolution, and the leak-path gate keeping automatic project_cid writes off). Adopted by citation rather than re-derived, resolving all 5 of the dispatch's numbered questions with no blocking ambiguity.

Dispatch territory names agent-system/extensions/sapience/merge-sources/claudemd.md, which does not exist; the real claudemd merge source is EXTENSION.md per manifest.json merge_targets. Plan redirects the edit target and forbids creating the literal path.

rules/sapience-write-path.md claims '14 files under the source store path, exactly three of which legitimately name the MCP write tools'. The 14 is exact; the three is under-counted -- a measured grep over those 14 instruction surfaces returns five (per-repo-scoping.md, review-gate-boundary.md, EXTENSION.md, index-entries.json, the rule file). Plan Phase 3 corrects the figure and the sanctioned-site list.

EXTENSION.md is exactly 60 lines against check-extension-docs.sh Rule U's hard 60-line ceiling (SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE defaults to hard), so the new context pointer has zero headroom. Isolated into its own phase with a before/after wc -l check so a net-positive edit fails there rather than as an unrelated Gate 3 failure later.

This task's dispatch territory names context/project/sapience/domain/per-repo-scoping.md, which is also in a concurrent sibling task's declared file_scope for this same /orchestrate cycle. Resolved by excluding that file from every phase and giving Ruling 3 a new dedicated domain record that cites it by heading instead; recorded as a follow-up that the cited subsection carries no forward pointer.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification measurement check caught two mis-claims in the first draft immediately: a fabricated suite name (a test file this plan will create but which does not exist yet, so the selector cannot return it) and an under-verifying suite list. Rephrasing both justifications to name verify-touched.sh over the declared Files to modify set, with no suite basenames inlined, cleared the plan to 0 warnings.

Phase 1's new, unreferenced context file (linked-repo-write-policy.md) correctly triggered verify-touched.sh's OWED-NOT-PAID fallback, running the full free-cost-class suite battery (98 suites) plus the normally-resolved 22-suite set; all passed except the one pre-existing, already-EXPECTED-flaky test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh timeout -- 0 NEW failures, confirming the scoped batch-gate-deferral tier was sufficient for this phase without a full verify-deploy.sh sweep.
Write tool created test-sapience-remember.sh without the executable bit; run-all.sh's deployed-tree run reported [SKIP] not executable until chmod +x was applied at the source and redeployed.

test-sapience-remember.sh's Case 6 (settings-fragment.json policy invariant) initially resolved the fragment via a SCRIPT_DIR-relative path, which fails when the suite runs from a deployed .claude/scripts/tests/ copy (the fragment has no standalone deployed file -- it is merge-targeted into .claude/settings.local.json). Fixed by resolving via common_test_ext_root(REPO_ROOT) instead, which works whether the suite runs from source or deployed tree.

sapience-publish.sh's ko subcommand already implemented the exact project-key runtime-resolution shape (binding cid -> GET /v1/people/projects -> matched key) needed for sapience-remember.sh, so Phase 2's core logic was a direct, low-risk copy rather than new design; byte-identical-output verification for the unlinked case passed on the first try.

generate-context-line-counts.sh's documented REPO_ROOT override let the Phase 3 line_count resync run directly from the source store with no redeploy detour; all three edited context files' line_count mismatches were corrected in one surgical --write pass with a clean, line_count-only diff.

Phase 4 (resolve-once pass-through): duplicating sapience-remember.sh's PROJECT-KEY RESOLUTION block directly inside postflight-sapience-notes.sh (rather than requiring a new flag on sapience-remember.sh itself, which was out of this phase's file_scope) let the whole feature land within the two declared Files to modify. New test cases 10/11 confirmed exactly one GET for a 3-note linked batch and zero GETs for an unlinked batch, both on the first run.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped '.claude-extensions.json' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 6's git-commit-phase.sh call dropped .claude-extensions.json from the phase commit despite __WHOLE_TREE__ being present in task 678's declared file_scope -- the Containment Self-Check does exact/ancestor string matching per entry and does not treat __WHOLE_TREE__ as a wildcard admitting deploy-headless.sh's own rewritten files. Recovered via the designed mechanical follow-up-commit trigger: the dropped path was deposited into .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope, and landed with a direct, scoped git-commit-scoped.sh call.

Phase 6's fixture-based linked-repo verification (scratch repo + .sapience/project.json binding + PATH-shadowing curl stub) exercised postflight-sapience-notes.sh end to end on the first attempt with zero debugging -- the fixture cid/key pair reused from the Phase 2 test suite and the deploy-root-guard.sh */.claude or */.opencode parent-directory check (which accepts any scratch tree shaped that way) meant the production script ran unmodified against a fully synthetic tree with no live-vault network reach.
